where: crates/harness/mcp/src/daemon.ts `SOCK`; every test that runs a cell
what: The daemon socket's path ignored HARNESS_HOME (`$HOME/.harness/harnessd.sock` unless HARNESS_SOCK was set), so a test or script that set only HARNESS_HOME to a scratch directory would still post its cells to, and run its `sh` through, the person's live daemon. I noticed only because the live socket exists on this Mac.
cost: ten minutes; no harm found, but any new test that ran a cell would have written `repl` objects into the live index
cause: two derivations of one path: the Rust daemon uses home().join("harnessd.sock"), the kernel had its own
whys: why possible: the kernel computed the socket path from $HOME, not from the state directory
why not caught: each test that ran cells remembered to set HARNESS_SOCK by hand
property: isolation from the live harness was each test's own job
class: a test or script reaching the person's live state because isolation is opt-in per file
prevention: SOCK() derives from HOME() (src/self.ts) as the daemon does; bunfig.toml preloads src/test-setup.ts, which gives every `bun test` run its own empty HARNESS_HOME and unsets HARNESS_SOCK and HARNESS_SESSION
